predecessors.name: Bahmani Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Bahmani taraf (province) of Bijapur, with its Konkan coast and Goa

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: the whole sultanate as corrected for 1683-1686, annexed after the siege of 1685-86

ledger.x: 1490: Yusuf Adil Shah makes Bijapur a de facto independent state, breaking away from the Bahmani Sultanate.
1504: Yusuf Adil Shah annexes Gulbarga.
1510: the Portuguese attack Goa.
November 1510: Goa passes to the Portuguese for good; 'the Portuguese again conquered it in November of that year'.
November 1510: Goa is lost to the Portuguese, who 'again conquered it in November of that year'.
19 May 1520: Vijayanagara wins at Raichur.
1530: Ismail Adil Shah recovers Raichur and Mudgal.
1534: Vijayanagara takes the Raichur Doab again.

c. 1547: Cliopatria adds about 15 cells of the northern Kanara coast to Bijapur. The Ibrahim Adil Shah I page confirms the movement in his reign (1535-1558) without a year or a place: 'considerable acquisitions were made in the south along the west coast' and 'The farthest point of Bijapur territory now extended south…

c. 1547: about 11 cells at the Solapur-Naldurg edge pass to Ahmadnagar. The Ibrahim Adil Shah I page says that in his reign 'while Bidar was conquered, Solapur and Kalyani were lost to Ahmadnagar' without years. The 1547 year and the cells are…
c. 1552: the Solapur-Naldurg strip returns to Bijapur in Cliopatria's shapes; no page opened dates it.
1561: Ahmadnagar returns Kaliyani.
1565: the Raichur Doab returns to Bijapur after Talikota.
1575: Ali Adil Shah I completes the conquest of the Carnatic.
1618: Bijapur loses Janjira.
1619: Bijapur annexes Bidar.
1636: Bijapur accepts Mughal suzerainty.
December 1638: Bijapur takes Bangalore.
1641: Bijapur's army takes Vellore.
1648: Gingee falls to Bijapur.
1656: Shivaji takes the Javali valley.
1657: the Mughals take Bidar.
1659: Ali Adil Shah II's campaign against Thanjavur begins.
10 November 1659: Shivaji destroys Afzal Khan's army and takes Pratapgad's country and Panhala.
22 September 1660: Shivaji hands Panhala back.
1663: the Thanjavur campaign ends ('captured Thanjavur and other cities from the Nayakas from 1659 to 1663').
1673: Shivaji retakes Panhala.
April 1675: Shivaji takes Ponda.
July 1675: Shivaji takes Kolhapur and Karwar.
1677: Shivaji invades Karnataka and seizes Vellore and Gingee.
November 1677: Shivaji takes the Mysore plateau.
April 1685: the 1636 tribute relation is over when Aurangzeb declares war.
April 1685: the Mughal siege of Bijapur begins ('15 April 1685 - 12 September 1686'; the army arrived in March 1685, Aurangzeb himself on 4 September 1686).
12 September 1686: Bijapur surrenders; 'The siege of Bijapur began in April 1685 and ended in September 1686 with a Mughal victory.'
12 September 1686: the Mughals annex the sultanate; Sikandar Adil Shah is 'bound in silver chains and presented before Aurangzeb'.
12 September 1686: the Adil Shahi sultanate ends.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa (1510)
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory: Goa taken in 1510, retaken by Yusuf Adil Shah two months later and conquered again in November 1510.

wars.name: Battle of Raichur
wars.outcome: Decisive Vijayanagara victory on 19 May 1520; Krishnadevaraya occupies Bijapur for a time.

wars.name: Vijayanagara-Bijapur Raichur Doab wars, 1529-1534
wars.outcome: Ismail Adil Shah recaptures Raichur and Mudgal in 1530; Vijayanagara seizes the Raichur Doab in 1534.

wars.name: Ahmadnagar-Bijapur wars over Solapur and Kaliyani
wars.outcome: Burhan Nizam Shah I's fourth invasion of 1553 reached nearly to Bijapur; Kaliyani returned to Bijapur in 1561; Hussain's 1563 siege of Kaliyani abandoned; 'Another conflict between Ahmednagar and Bijapur arose in 1567', a stalemate.

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates on 23 January 1565; 'The Bijapur Sultanate reaped maximum gains' (Talikota page); the Raichur Doab was returned to Bijapur (Adil Shahi page).

wars.name: Bijapur-Portuguese war of 1570-71
wars.outcome: Ali Adil Shah I's conflict with the Portuguese, which he lost; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Ali Adil Shah I's Carnatic campaign
wars.outcome: Bijapur conquers Adoni and much of the Carnatic; land gained by 1576 doubled the sultanate's holdings.

wars.name: Mughal-Bijapur wars, 1631-1657
wars.outcome: Shah Jahan besieges Bijapur in 1631 (first Mughal invasion); in 1636 Bijapur signs a treaty to pay tribute; Aurangzeb captures Bidar and other forts in 1657.

wars.name: Bijapur's Karnataka campaigns under Shahaji
wars.outcome: Bijapur takes Bangalore (December 1638), Vellore (1641) and Gingee (1648, with Golconda's help).

wars.name: Bijapur-Maratha wars under Shivaji
wars.outcome: Shivaji takes Javali (1656), defeats Afzal Khan (10 November 1659), holds and returns Panhala (1659-60), retakes it (1673), and takes Ponda, Karwar and Kolhapur (1675) and Vellore and Gingee (1677).

wars.name: Bijapur's Thanjavur campaign
wars.outcome: Ali Adil Shah II 'captured Thanjavur and other cities from the Nayakas from 1659 to 1663'.

wars.name: Siege of Bijapur
wars.outcome: Mughal victory on 12 September 1686: the sultanate is annexed and Sikandar Adil Shah captured; the Marathas under Sambhaji had supported Bijapur.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary survey or treaty line for Bijapur (the 1636 treaty with the Mughals is dated, not delimited).
